name: Lateral occipital cortex, inferior division
summary: The inferior lateral occipital cortex is the lower part of the outer surface of the occipital lobe, below the lateral occipital sulcus and above the preoccipital notch, continuous in front with the temporo-occipital cortex. It contains the shape- and object-selective cortex of the lateral occipital complex and part of the extrastriate body area, the beginning of the ventral visual stream that identifies what is seen. It is supplied by the posterior cerebral artery with a middle cerebral artery contribution laterally, and its lesions cause apperceptive agnosia and contralateral upper quadrant defects; the region is a frequent site of visual auras and of the hallucinations of Charles Bonnet syndrome.

anatomy.location: Lower lateral occipital surface between the lateral occipital sulcus above and the inferior margin of the hemisphere at the preoccipital notch, behind the inferior temporal gyrus and lateral to the occipital fusiform gyrus.

afferents.from: Primary visual cortex and lingual gyrus

function: Neurons of the lateral occipital complex respond to the shape of objects regardless of the cues that define them, whether luminance edges, texture or motion, and represent bodies and body parts in an adjacent patch; this shape information feeds the fusiform and inferior temporal recognition areas. The region is retinotopic for the contralateral upper field and it contributes to the perception of depth and of figure from ground. Damage produces apperceptive agnosia with inability to copy or match shapes despite intact acuity, and release phenomena produce formed hallucinations of objects and figures when the input is lost.

bestView.label: inferior lateral occipital cortex above the preoccipital notch

imaging.normalAppearance: Lateral occipital cortex below the lateral occipital sulcus on axial images through the level of the atria and below, behind the temporo-occipital junction.

pathology.finding: Restricted diffusion of the inferior lateral occipital cortex with a contralateral upper quadrantanopia and impaired shape perception.
Formed visual hallucinations of people or patterns in a patient with visual loss from any cause; imaging excludes a structural occipital lesion.
Focal FLAIR-bright cortex at the lateral occipital surface in a patient with visual seizures.

lesionEffects.mechanism: Loss of shape integration in the lateral occipital complex
Involvement of the ventral extrastriate cortex or the lower optic radiation
Release or ictal activation of object-selective visual cortex

examination: Copy and match simple shapes and letters
Ask about hallucinations of people, animals or patterns and whether the patient knows they are unreal
pearls: Charles Bonnet hallucinations are unreal and known to be unreal by the patient; they are a sign of visual loss, not psychosis
An apperceptive agnosic cannot copy a drawing; an associative agnosic copies it slavishly and still cannot recognize it
The lower lateral occipital cortex represents the upper visual field

pitfalls: Hallucinations in a patient with poor vision should prompt an eye examination and an occipital MRI before antipsychotics
